text: CHAPTER OF THE BERGEN TOWN CODE DRAFT 10/26 DATA CENTERS AND CRYPTOCURRENCY FACILITIES Authority. This chapter is adopted pursuant to the New York State Constitution, Article IX, Town Law §2(c)(6) and (10), New York Statute of Local Governments, § 10 (1) and (7); sections 261 through 264 and section 10 of the Municipal Home Rule Law of the State of New York, which authorizes the Town of Bergen to adopt zoning provisions that advance and protect the health, safety and welfare of the community. Purpose and intent. A. This chapter is adopted to advance and protect the public health, safety, welfare, and quality of life of the Town of Bergen by creating regulations for the installation and use of data centers and cryptocurrency facilities, with the following objectives: (1) To provide a regulatory scheme for the designation of properties suitable for the location, construction and operation of data centers and cryptocurrency facilities, thereby directing development away from agricultural lands, sensitive environmental resources and residential neighborhoods and areas that currently have or can acquire the infrastructure necessary to support such facilities. (2) To ensure compatible land uses in the vicinity of the areas affected by data centers and cryptocurrency facilities. (3) To mitigate and limit environmental impacts (heat discharge, stormwater runoff and adverse effects on air and water quality) of data centers and cryptocurrency facilities on environmental resources, such as important agricultural lands, forests, wildlife and other protected resources. (4) To create synergy between data center/cryptocurrency facility development and other stated goals of Bergen pursuant to its Comprehensive Plan. (5) To preserve the character of the community by assuring appropriate design, siting, screening and other appropriate measures to limit the visual impact and avoid incompatible land use conflicts. (6) To prevent nuisance conditions such as excessive noise, vibration, and light pollution that could impact nearby residences, businesses, or agricultural operations. (7) To protect infrastructure capacity by ensuing that electrical, water, and wastewater systems can reliably meet the needs of these facilities without compromising service to other users. B. This zoning ordinance does not supersede any other state or federal regulation pertaining to electrical storage laws. Any conflict between this chapter and state law and federal law and/or utility regulation shall be resolved by application of state law and federal law and/or utility regulations. Definitions. ACCESSORY DATA CENTER USE/CONTAINMENT STRUCTURE — A building, or structure, or partial use of a building or structure, used to store, manage, process or transmit digital data for business uses, including computers, network equipment, systems, servers, and other associated components related to the digital data storage and operations that is secondary, subordinate and customarily incidental to and located on the same lot as the principal use of a property. Such a use cannot dominate the property or operate as an independent principal use. DATA CENTER — An industrial use facility that is primarily used for the storage, management, processing, and transmission of digital data, and which houses computer or network equipment, systems, servers, appliances, and other associated components related to the digital data storage and processing as a principal land use on a parcel. Equipment and accessories customary to data centers including but not limited to air handlers, power generators, water cooling and storage facilities, utility substations, and other associated utility infrastructure shall also be considered part of a data center. Accessory structures or rooms that house equipment and staff to serve an on-site business or office shall also be considered a data center. COMMERCIAL CYRYPTOCURRENCY MINING- The process where a global network of computers running special software to solve codes works to ensure that transactions are legitimate and added correctly to the digital database and new cryptocurrency is added into circulation through the use of server clusters that require a high energy consumption service. CRYPTOCURRENCY — A digitally generated currency secured in a manner making it difficult to counterfeit or double spend. CRYPTOCURRENCY DATA MINE - A specific type of data center using a facility or use of land, buildings, or structures where computing equipment is used to solve complex mathematical algorithms in connection with verifying and adding transactions to a blockchain or other distributed ledger, commonly known as cryptocurrency mining. For purposes of this law, a cryptocurrency data mining operation shall be considered a distinct land use, different from a “data center” as defined in this section. SENSITIVE RECEPTOR - Schools, preschools, day care centers, in-home daycares, health facilities such as hospitals, long term care facilities, retirement and nursing homes, community centers, places of worship, playgrounds, parks (excluding trails), campgrounds, dormitories, and any residence where such residence is not located on a parcel with an existing industrial, commercial, or unpermitted use. SERVER CLUSTER- A group of three or more computers that are connected with each other and operate closely to act as a single computer to be used for the purpose of cryptocurrency mining. UNREASONABLE NOISE - Any sound, which by reason of its volume, pitch, frequency, duration, repetition, character of the area, or time of occurrence is excessive or unwanted or sound that interferes with the normal use and enjoyment of property, and which annoys, disturbs, injures or endangers the comfort, repose, health, peace or safety of a reasonable person of normal sensitivities, or which causes injury to animal life or damage to property or business. Unreasonable noise includes, but it did not limit to, continuous or tonal sounds, impulsive or intermittent noises, and low-frequency vibrations. Applicability. The requirements of this section shall apply to all data centers, cryptocurrency mines, and accessory data center uses proposed or modified in the Town of Bergen after the effective date of this chapter. All data centers, cryptocurrency mines, and accessory data center uses as defined shall require both Site Plan Review and approval and a Special Use Permit review and approval. General Requirements. A. Data Center, Cryptocurrency facilities and accessory buildings shall be allowed as accessory use in the Town of Bergen’s Industrial Zones. All uses shall be subject to review and approval with a Special Use Permit and Site Plan Review. B. A building permit issued by the Bergen Code Enforcement Officer shall be required for construction or modification of any data center, cryptocurrency mine and accessory data center. An electrical inspection must be conducted by an approved electrical inspection agency for Bergen. C. Issuance of approvals by the Bergen Planning Board which shall include review pursuant to the State Environmental Quality Review Act, including ECL Article 8 and its implementing regulations at NYCRR Part 617 (“SEQRA). D. All data centers, cryptocurrency mines and accessory data centers battery energy storage systems buildings, and all other buildings or structures are subject to the Uniform Code and/or the Energy Code shall be designed, erected, and installed in accordance with all applicable provisions of the Uniform Code, all applicable provisions of the Energy Code, and all applicable provisions of the codes, regulations, and industry standards as referenced in the Uniform Code, the Energy Code, and the Town of Bergen Town Code. E. All data centers, cryptocurrency mines and accessory data center buildings or structures shall comply with the International Fire Code, NFPA 70, NFPA 855, and other relevant State and Federal codes and regulations. Site Plan and Special Use Permit Application Requirements for Data Centers/ Cryptocurrency Mines and Accessory Data/Cryptocurrency Center Uses A. All accessory data/cryptocurrency center uses shall be subject to review and approval with a Special Use Permit and Site Plan Review. A new site plan review and renewal of the special use permit shall be required for any physical expansion of any pre-existing data/cryptocurrency containment structures. In addition to other submission requirements of Bergen Town Code Chapter 475, an application for such facilities shall also include the following: 1. A narrative description of the nature of the on-site activities and operations, including the market area served by the facility, the hours of operation of the facility, the total number of employees on each shift, the times, frequencies, and types of vehicle trips generated, the types of materials stored and the duration period of storage of materials. Ne . A site plan of the property that indicates the location of proposed improvements, flood plains, wetlands, streams, and cultural and historic resources on the property and within 500 feet of the boundaries of the property, as well as appropriate fencing and/or other reasonable steps to ensure safety from electrical hazards and identifying a power source for the operation. ies) Data clearly articulates water needs, use, availability, recycling and/or release procedures, and local and regional impacts on water resources. 4. Data that clearly articulates electrical needs and sources. 5. An evaluation of the potential impacts of the proposed use, both positive and negative, upon: (a) Emergency services and fire protection, (b)Sewage disposal (c) Solid waste disposal 6. A narrative description of any environmental impacts that are likely to be generated (e.g., odor, noise, smoke, dust, trash, glare, heat islands, vibration, electrical disturbance, wastewater, stormwater, solid waste, etc.) and specific measures employed to mitigate or eliminate any negative impacts. The applicant shall provide further evidence that the impacts generated by the proposed use fall within acceptable levels, as regulated by applicable laws and ordinances. B. Application for any data center, cryptocurrency mine and our accessory data center buildings must be made to and approved by the Bergen Planning Board, where it must meet the guidelines as defined herein and shall be: 1. Reviewed by the Bergen Planning Board for completeness. An application shall be complete when it addresses all matters listed herein, including, but not limited to, compliance with the Uniform Code, the Energy Code, addressing matters relating to floodplain, utility lines, electrical circuitry, signage, lighting, vegetation, tree cutting, noise, decommissioning, site plan considerations, special use considerations, ownership changes, safety, emergency operation plan, easements, permit time frame and abandonment. Applicants shall be advised within 15 business days as to the status of the application. i) Subject to a public hearing to hear all comments for and against the application. The Bergen Planning Board shall have a notice printed in at least once in the official newspaper so designated by the Town Board at least five days before such hearing, Applicants shall deliver the notice by first class mail to adjoining landowners or landowners within 1,000 feet of the property at least 10 days prior to such hearing. Proof of mailing shall be provided to the Bergen Planning Board at the public hearing. ies) Referred to the Genesee County Planning Department pursuant to General Municipal Law § 239-m if required. 4. Upon closing of the public hearing, the Bergen Planning Board shall take action on the application within 62 days of the public hearing, which can include approval, approval with conditions, or denial. The sixty- two-day period may be extended upon consent of both the Bergen Planning Board and the applicant. 5. Upon approval of the Bergen Planning Board, an application for a building permit is to be made to the Bergen Code Enforcement Officer. Design and Siting Standards. In addition to the Site Plan considerations and Special Use standards, the following design and sitting standards shall be met by all data centers, cryptocurrency mines, and accessory data center uses: (1) Building Placement and Siting. a) Data center or cryptocurrency facility must be located within the Town of Bergen’s industrial zones. b) Data Centers, cryptocurrency mines and accessory data center uses that visually approximate commercial office building is encouraged. c) No container storage structures such as but not limited to shipping containers, shall be used to house a data center. d) There shall be no blank, windowless wall facing any private or public street. e) All mechanical equipment shall be shown on any proposed site plan and must be fully screened on all sides with a design, materials, details, and treatment compatible with those used on the principal fagade of the building. f) No ground mounted mechanical equipment shall be located in any required front yard. (2) Off-street Loading Areas. Loading bays are permitted to be located on only | fagade but shall not be located on the front facade. (3) Area and Bulk Standards a) Only one data center or cryptocurrency mine shall be allowed in each of the town’s Interchange INT-R, Interchange INT-I and Industrial I district. b) The minimum required lot size shall be 2 acres. c) The maximum height shall not exceed 35 feet. d) The minimum road frontage shall be 150’. e) All buildings and structures associated with data centers or cryptocurrency mines shall maintain a minimum 100-foot setback from all property lines. (4) Parking. There should be one parking space for each employee per shift. All ADA requirements shall also be met. (5) Lighting. All exterior lighting, whether building mounted or pole is mounted, shall be designed and constructed with cutoff and fully shielded fixtures that direct light downward and into the interior of the property and away from adjacent roads and properties. No outdoor lighting used for the data center shall create light that exceeds 0.1 footcandle at any adjacent residential property, or 0.5 footeandle when adjacent to any non-residential use. No light pole shall exceed 18” in height. Except for safety lighting, lighting for parking areas shall be automatically turned off by 10:00 pm. 6) Fencing. If security fencing is provided, such fencing shall be effectively screened using vegetation placed ro os o 5S 2 > oe outside the fence and outside of the road right-of-way. Security fencing shall not exceed ten feet in height. See also (8) below. (7) Signage. Data centers shall have one building-mounted and one ground-mounted sign. There shall be a maximum total sign area of 32 square feet. Additionally, a sign listing all 24-hour contact information shall be provided on site in a location easily accessible to emergency responders. (8) Screening. Screening shall be required whenever a data center, cryptocurrency mine, and accessory data center use is adjacent to a residential use or a residential zoning district. The Planning Board may waive the screening when the data center is not adjacent to a residence or a residential district. b) Use of existing vegetation for landscaping and screening is strongly encouraged and may be substituted for new berms and plantings when approved by the Planning Board. c) When fencing has been provided, screening shall be a minimum depth of 8 feet of vegetation when the data center abuts residential properties or a residential zoning district. d) All fencing provided along road frontage shall be landscaped. E. Performance Standards. (1) Noise and Heat (a) Data center/cryptocurrency mining operation may not cause unreasonable noise that causes adverse or detrimental effects to adjoining tenants, licensees, owners and/or residents and that diminishes the quality of life or increases the costs of operating their business or maintaining their homes. An acoustical study prepared by a professional acoustical engineer shall be required as part of the site plan and special use application that demonstrates that the use, including all its components, will not produce a noise level of 60 decibels and above measured at the lot lines of the premises where the facility is located. b) On property adjacent to existing residential development, or to a zoning district permitting residential uses, all mechanical equipment associated with data center, cryptocurrency mine, and accessory data center uses located on the property, whether on a roof top, on the ground level, or elsewhere on the exterior of the property, shall be fully screened on all four sides by an acoustical barrier using methods including but not limited to louvers, enclosures, fan selection and speed controls, use of restricted generator testing hours, or changing equipment yard orientation. c) The Planning Board and/or Town Board may require additional sound mitigation if the acoustical study indicates potential impacts to sensitive receptors, and when increases in ambience noise in excess of 3 dB are likely to occur. (2) Containment structure requirements. (a) Containment structures. The containment structure shall be at least 700 square feet, permanently affixed, and not be created solely by shipping containers or tother temporary buildings. Application for any data center, cryptocurrency mine and our accessory data center buildings must be made to and approved by the Bergen Planning Board, where it must meet the guidelines as defined herein and shall be: 1. Reviewed by the Bergen Planning Board for completeness. An application shall be complete when it addresses all matters listed herein, including, but not limited to, compliance with the Uniform Code, the Energy Code, addressing matters relating to floodplain, utility lines, electrical circuitry, signage, lighting, vegetation, tree cutting, noise, decommissioning, site plan considerations, special use considerations, ownership changes, safety, emergency operation plan, easements, permit time frame and abandonment. Applicants shall be advised within 15 business days as to the status of the application. i) Subject to a public hearing to hear all comments for and against the application. The Bergen Planning Board shall have a notice printed in at least once in the official newspaper so designated by the Town Board at least five days before such hearing, Applicants shall deliver the notice by first class mail to adjoining landowners or landowners within 1,000 feet of the property at least 10 days prior to such hearing. Proof of mailing shall be provided to the Bergen Planning Board at the public hearing. ies) Referred to the Genesee County Planning Department pursuant to General Municipal Law § 239-m if required. 4. Upon closing of the public hearing, the Bergen Planning Board shall take action on the application within 62 days of the public hearing, which can include approval, approval with conditions, or denial. The sixty- two-day period may be extended upon consent of both the Bergen Planning Board and the applicant. 5. Upon approval of the Bergen Planning Board, an application for a building permit is to be made to the Bergen Code Enforcement Officer. Design and Siting Standards. In addition to the Site Plan considerations and Special Use standards, the following design and sitting standards shall be met by all data centers, cryptocurrency mines, and accessory data center uses: (1) Building Placement and Siting. a) Data center or cryptocurrency facility must be located within the Town of Bergen’s industrial zones. b) Data Centers, cryptocurrency mines and accessory data center uses that visually approximate commercial office building is encouraged. c) No container storage structures such as but not limited to shipping containers, shall be used to house a data center. d) There shall be no blank, windowless wall facing any private or public street. e) All mechanical equipment shall be shown on any proposed site plan and must be fully screened on all sides with a design, materials, details, and treatment compatible with those used on the principal fagade of the building. f) No ground mounted mechanical equipment shall be located in any required front yard. (2) Off-street Loading Areas. Loading bays are permitted to be located on only | fagade but shall not be located on the front facade. (3) Area and Bulk Standards a) Only one data center or cryptocurrency mine shall be allowed in each of the town’s Interchange INT-R, Interchange INT-I and Industrial I district. b) The minimum required lot size shall be 2 acres. c) The maximum height shall not exceed 35 feet. d) The minimum road frontage shall be 150’. e) All buildings and structures associated with data centers or cryptocurrency mines shall maintain a minimum 100-foot setback from all property lines. (4) Parking. There should be one parking space for each employee per shift. All ADA requirements shall also be met. (5) Lighting. All exterior lighting, whether building mounted or pole is mounted, shall be designed and constructed with cutoff and fully shielded fixtures that direct light downward and into the interior of the property and away from adjacent roads and properties. No outdoor lighting used for the data center shall create light that exceeds 0.1 footcandle at any adjacent residential property, or 0.5 footeandle when adjacent to any non-residential use. No light pole shall exceed 18” in height. Except for safety lighting, lighting for parking areas shall be automatically turned off by 10:00 pm. 6) Fencing. If security fencing is provided, such fencing shall be effectively screened using vegetation placed ro os o 5S 2 > oe outside the fence and outside of the road right-of-way. Security fencing shall not exceed ten feet in height. See also (8) below. (7) Signage. Data centers shall have one building-mounted and one ground-mounted sign. There shall be a maximum total sign area of 32 square feet. Additionally, a sign listing all 24-hour contact information shall be provided on site in a location easily accessible to emergency responders. (8) Screening. Screening shall be required whenever a data center, cryptocurrency mine, and accessory data center use is adjacent to a residential use or a residential zoning district. The Planning Board may waive the screening when the data center is not adjacent to a residence or a residential district. b) Use of existing vegetation for landscaping and screening is strongly encouraged and may be substituted for new berms and plantings when approved by the Planning Board. c) When fencing has been provided, screening shall be a minimum depth of 8 feet of vegetation when the data center abuts residential properties or a residential zoning district. d) All fencing provided along road frontage shall be landscaped. text: VILLAGE/TOWN OF MOUNT KISCO PROPOSED LOCAL LAW #03 OF 2026 A LOCAL LAW TO AMEND CHAPTER 96 – TAXATION OF THE CODE OF THE VILLAGE/TOWN OF MOUNT KISCO Be it enacted by the Village Board of the Village/Town of Mount Kisco of the County of Westchester as follows: Additions are reflected with Underlining, Deletions are reflected within Strikethrough Section 1. Legislative Intent. The Board of Trustees finds that the New York State Legislature has amended § 458-a of the Real Property Tax Law (RPTL) to authorize municipalities to adopt a full exemption from real property taxation for the primary residence of seriously disabled veterans meeting specified eligibility requirements. The Board further finds that the Village has long recognized the sacrifices made by veterans and their families. Consistent with that recognition, the Board desires to provide the fullest exemption authorized by law to those veterans whose service-connected disabilities have resulted in permanent and total disability. The Board also desires to increase the maximum exemption allowable for veterans, combat zone veterans, and disabled veterans under RPTL § 458-a for whom RPTL § 458-a. 11. does not apply The purpose of this Local Law is to amend Chapter 96 of the Code of the Village/Town of Mount Kisco to adopt the optional exemption authorized by RPTL § 458-a. 11., and to adopt a Veterans Alternative Exemption that will increase the maximum exemption allowable authorized by RPTL § 458-a. 2.(d)(ii). Section 2. Authority. This local law is adopted pursuant to Real Property Tax Law § 458-a. Section 3. The Code of the Village/Town of Mount Kisco Chapter 96 Taxation, Article III Real Property Tax Exemptions, is hereby amended to add a new § 96-16.3 Veterans; alternative tax exemption, as follows: § 96-16.3. Veterans; alternative tax exemption. A. Grant of exemption. Pursuant to § 458-a of the Real Property Tax Law (RPTL), qualifying residential real property as defined therein shall be eligible for the veterans alternative exemption as authorized therein. B. Maximum exemption amounts. The Village/Town of Mount Kisco hereby grants the following maximum exemption amounts as authorized by RPTL § 458-a: (1) War Veteran Exemption: $75,000 (2) Combat Veteran Exemption: $50,000. This exemption is in addition to any exemption granted under (1) of this subsection as authorized and permitted under RPTL § 458-a. (3) Disabled Veteran Exemption: $250,000 C. Seriously Disabled Veterans Exemption. Pursuant to RPTL § 458-a. 11., the Village/Town of Mount Kisco hereby grants the full real property tax exemption for seriously disabled veterans authorized therein. Section 4. The Code of the Village/Town of Mount Kisco Chapter 96 Taxation, Article III Real Property Tax Exemptions, is hereby amended to add a new § 96-17.3 Qualifications for veterans; alternative exemption. § 96-17.3. Qualifications for veterans; alternative exemption. Eligibility for the exemptions authorized by § 96-16.3 shall be determined in accordance with Real Property Tax Law (RPTL) § 458-a. No exemption as provided for in § 96-16.3 shall be granted unless all of the applicable qualifications and requirements of RPTL § 458-a are met. Section 5. The Code of the Village/Town of Mount Kisco Chapter 96 Taxation, Article III Real Property Tax Exemptions, is hereby amended to add a new § 96-18.3 Application for veterans; alternative exemption. § 96-18.3. Application for veterans; alternative exemption. Applications for the exemptions authorized by § 96-16.3 shall be filed with the Village/Town of Mount Kisco Assessor's Office, which shall determine eligibility for, and administer, such exemptions in accordance with Real Property Tax Law (RPTL) § 458-a. Section 6. The Code of the Village/Town of Mount Kisco Chapter 96 Taxation, Article III Real Property Tax Exemptions, § 96-16. Exemption granted, is hereby amended to be renamed as follows: § 96-16. Senior citizen Eexemption granted. Section 7. Following adoption of this Local Law, the Village Clerk shall notify the New York State Department of Veterans' Services in accordance with Real Property Tax Law (RPTL) § 458-a. 11.(d). Section 8. In the event of any conflict or inconsistency between the provisions of this Local Law and any other provisions of the Code of the Village/Town of Mount Kisco, the provisions of this Local Law shall prevail to the extent necessary to give full force and effect to its provisions. Section 9. If any clause, sentence, paragraph, section or part of this Local Law is declared by a Court of competent jurisdiction to be invalid, such judgment shall not affect, impair or invalidate the remainder thereof, but shall be confined in its operation to said clause, sentence, paragraph, section or part of this Local Law. Section 10. This Local Law shall take effect immediately upon filing in the office of the Secretary of State in accordance with Municipal Home Rule Law Section 27. text: TOWN OF NORTH ELBA LOCAL LAW __ OF 2026 ESTABLISHING A MORATORIUM ON BATTERY ENERGY STORAGE SYSTEMS BE IT ENACTED BY THE NORTH ELBA TOWN BOARD AS FOLLOWS: 1. Title and Authority – This Local Law shall be known as the Town of North Elba Battery Energy Storage Systems Moratorium. It is adopted pursuant to Municipal Home Rule Law §10 and Town Law Article 16. 2. Purpose – The Town Board recognizes that Battery Energy Storage Systems facilities are a component to the promotion of renewable energy sources, however, the technology of these systems is still in its infancy. Public health, safety, and welfare are some of the highest priorities in the Town, causing the Town Board to want to have the ability to study the approach to and impacts from the development of Battery Energy Storage Systems facilities. This Moratorium is necessary in order to temporarily restrict the development of Battery Energy Storage Systems so that the Town Board may thoroughly consider the impacts of such uses, their appropriate locations in the community and how to allow for appropriate development of such facilities within the Town’s land use development and zoning objectives. The Town Board has determined that this would best enhance and protect the health, safety and welfare of the citizens of the Town of North Elba. 3. Definitions – “Battery Energy Storage System” means one or more devices, assembled together, capable of storing energy derived from any source including without limitation solar or wind sources, to be stored and then released at a future time. 4. Moratorium – The Town of North Elba hereby imposes a one-year Moratorium on the construction, establishment, installation, review or approval of any Battery Energy Storage Systems after the date that this Local Law takes effect. During the pendency of this Moratorium, there shall be no construction nor permits issued nor applications considered by the Town, its Officials, Boards or Departments for the construction, installation or use of Battery Energy Storage Systems. 5. Extensions – This Moratorium may be extended for such additional periods as the Town Board may determine to be necessary to protect the public health, safety and welfare of the citizens of the Town of North Elba and accomplish the stated purposes and intent of this Local Law. 6. Variance Procedure – The Town Board shall have the power, after a Public Hearing, to vary or modify the application of any provision of this Local Law upon its determination that strict application of this Local Law would impose extraordinary hardship upon an applicant and that the variance granted would not adversely affect the health, safety or welfare of the citizens of the Town or significantly conflict with the general purposes and intent of this Local Law. Any request for a variance shall be in writing and filed with the Town Clerk. The Town Board shall conduct a Public Hearing on the application on not less than five (5) days’ public notice and shall make its decision within thirty (30) days after the close of the Public Hearing. Any project which is granted a variance from this Local Law shall be subject to all requirements under the Town Code which would have been applicable to the project if the Moratorium had not been adopted and the prohibitions set forth in Paragraph 4 of this Local Law shall not apply to such project. 7. Severability – The invalidity of any clause, sentence, paragraph or provision of this Local Law shall not invalidate any other clause, sentence, paragraph or part thereof. 8. Effective Date – This Local Law shall take effect upon filing by the Office of the New York Secretary of State. TOWN OF NORTH ELBA NOTICE OF PUBLIC HEARING ON PROPOSED LOCAL LAW NO. __ OF 2026 ESTABLISHING A MORATORIUM ON BATTERY ENERGY STORAGE SYSTEMS NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that the North Elba Town Board will hold a Public Hearing on OCTOBER 13, 2026, beginning at 5:15 pm at the North Elba Town Hall, 2693 Main Street, Lake Placid, New York, concerning proposed Local Law No. __ of 2026. The proposed Local Law would establish a one-year moratorium on any Battery Energy Storage Systems facility in the Town of North Elba. A Battery Energy Storage Systems facility is defined as one or more devices, assembled, capable of storing energy derived from any source, including solar or wind sources, to be stored and then released at a future time. Copies of the proposed Local Law are on file in the Town Clerk’s Office. All interested parties will be given an opportunity to be heard. title: Local Law # 5 of 2026
text: TOWN OF SALEM-COUNTY OF WASHINGTON LOCAL LAW #5 OF 2026 A LOCAL LAW TO OVERRIDE THE TAX LEVY LIMIT ESTABLISHED IN GENERAL MUNICIPAL LAW 3-c BE IT ENACTED by the Town Board of the Town of Salem, Washington County, New York, as follows: Section 1. Legislative Intent: It is the intent of this Local Law to override the limit on the amount of real property taxes that may be levied by the Town pursuant to General Municipal Law § 3-c, and to allow the Town of Salem to adopt a budget for the fiscal year beginning January 1, 2027 & ending December 31, 2027, that requires a real property tax levy in excess of the “tax levy limit” as defined by General Municipal Law § 3-c. Section 2. Authority: This Local Law is adopted pursuant to subdivision 5 of General Municipal Law § 3-c, which expressly authorizes the Town Board to override the tax levy limit by the adoption of a Local Law approved by vote of sixty percent (60%) of the town board. Section 3. Tax Levy Limit Override: The Town Board of the Town of Salem, County of Washington, is hereby authorized to adopt a budget for the fiscal year 2027 that requires a real property tax levy in excess of the amount otherwise prescribed in General Municipal Law, §3-c. Section 4. Severability: If any clause, sentence, paragraph, subdivision, or part of this Local Law or the application thereof to any person, firm or corporation, or circumstance, shall be adjusted by any court of competent jurisdiction to be invalid or unconstitutional, such order or judgment shall not affect, impair, or invalidate the remainder thereof, but shall be confined in its operation to the clause, sentence, paragraph, subdivision, or part of this Local Law or in its application to the person, individual, firm or corporation or circumstance, directly involved in the controversy in which such judgment or order shall be rendered. Section 5. Effective date: This Local Law shall take effect immediately upon filing with the Secretary of State.

Public Opening Comments: Opening Board Meeting Remarks: | want to update everyone on where we are with respect to Gooseneck Pond. On September 29" a group of us met with Marlene Martin and Alec Betancourt, from the New York State Department of Health, to discuss our ongoing plans for using Gooseneck Pond as a water source for the town. During the meeting we presented the work that the task team has been focused on, including an updated Map Plan Report (MPR) which Greg Swart’s, Suozzo & Doty Engineering, is preparing. In addition, we reviewed our three phased approach for bringing Gooseneck into compliance with the drinking water standards using UV disinfection, Chlorination and Filtration. We also discussed formation of a water district for the 107 homes in the Chilson Hill, Eagle Lake area, blending of waters from the Streetroad and Gooseneck systems, and our future work on the infrastructure related to Gooseneck. The exchange from both sides during this meeting was very positive and we will continue to work on opening lines of communication with the New York State Departments of Health, and Environmental Conservation, the Federal Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), and the Federal Court system. ROLL CALL VOTE: To: Ticonderoga Town Board Re: Water and Sewer EDU Determination-Formal Objection Following Denial of Appeal Members of the Town Board: I am submitting this statement concerning the Town's determination assigning two water EDUs and two sewer EDUs to my commercial property in downtown Ticonderoga. I previously appealed that determination to the Town Board. The Board denied my appeal by Resolution #262-2026, and the increased EDU classification became effective October 1, 2026. I continue to object to that determination and am submitting this statement to formally preserve my objections and to address issues that remain unresolved following the denial of my appeal. The property has a single commercial tenant and only one bathroom. Its actual use and demand on the water and sewer systems do not appear to provide a factual basis for doubling the property's EDU assessment. More importantly, I have requested records from the Town concerning the legal authority and uniform application of this classification. Those requests include the ordinance, resolution, rate schedule, policy, or other authority establishing the asserted two-EDU minimum for commercial properties, as well as EDU classifications and supporting records for comparable commercial properties within the Town. These records are material because the justification provided for my property's classification has been that commercial properties are subject to a two-EDU base. If that is the Town's policy, there should be clear legal authority establishing it and evidence that the same standard is being applied consistently to similarly situated commercial properties. If comparable commercial properties are being assessed differently, the Town should be able to identify the objective distinctions that justify those differences. Accordingly, I respectfully request that the Town Board: 1. Provide the specific legal authority establishing the two-EDU minimum that the Town applied to my property; 2. Complete the production of the records | have requested concerning EDU classifications and comparable properties; 3. Explain the objective criteria used to determine EDU classifications and how those criteria were applied to my property; 4. Suspend collection of the additional EDU charges while these outstanding records and classification issues are resolved; and 5. Reconsider Resolution #262-2026 if the requested records demonstrate that the asserted two-EDU standard is not supported by the governing law or has not been applied uniformly. Nothing in this statement should be construed as acceptance of the two-EDU classification or a waiver of any rights or remedies available to me concerning the determination, the denial of my appeal, or the Town's response to my records requests. Because I am presently outside New York, I intend to participate remotely in the October 8 meeting if permitted. Please distribute this statement to every member of the Town Board and include it in the official record and minutes of the October 8, 2026, Town Board meeting. Respectfully, William Harbour Property Owner Human Services - Youth LB Human Services - Seniors HT Health Insurance JO Contract Negotiations JO Cable T.V. text: DRAFT MINUTES LEWIS COUNTY PLANNING BOARD October 15, 2026 (1) Call to Order: Vice-Chairman Lehman called the regular meeting of the Lewis County Planning Board to order at 2:35 p.m. in the Basement Conference Room #030 at the Lewis County Courthouse, Lowville, New York. Mr. Lehman requested roll call. (2) Roll Call: Board Members Present: John Lehman, Donald Cook, John Reed, Jessica Moser, and Larry Dolhof. Staff Present: Lauryn Schell, Community Development Specialist; Casandra Buell, Director of Planning & Community Development; Grace Metzler, Grant Manager; Roxanne Turck, Naturally Lewis; Ben Manning, Building and Code Enforcement. Public Present: None. (3) Reading and Approval of Minutes: The draft August 20, 2026 meeting minutes were received and reviewed before the meeting. Mr. Lehman wanted to make sure that the minutes clearly defined all motions, seconders, voting outcomes, and any recusals, and that the meeting minutes should be amended to document unanimous and non-unanimous actions accurately. Ms. Buell reviewed the August 20th meeting minutes and found that a few of the actions did require clarity and that she will make those updates prior to posting the final versions. Mr. Cook moved to approve the minutes; Mr. Lehman seconded, and the motion carried unanimously. (4) Correspondence and Communication:  APA-Public Notice-Variance Application Received- Terry Steiner - Town of Croghan- Construction of a 10’ x 20’ deck attached to the shoreline side of a pre-1973 single-family dwelling within 100’ of the mean high water mark of Long Pond and within the West Branch Oswegatchie Recreational River Area.  APA-Major Project Public Notice- Application Completed- Ann Yost/Gerald Lucas - Town of Watson- Construction of a 120 +/- sq. ft dry-land boathouse consisting of a canopy supported by six 5-inch diameter poles and a timber retaining wall and accessed by twin pontoon roller ramps extending within the mean high-water mark.  APA-Certificate for Certain Minor Regulated Activities in APA Jurisdictional Freshwater Wetlands – Bryant Bridge Road / Town of Diana. The Board had no comments to submit regarding the correspondence provided. Page 1 of 9 (5) Report of Special Committees: 239-m Review Mr. Lehman introduced the first review. Jessica Moser moved to approve with the conditions and non-binding notes, which was seconded by Don Cook. Ms. Buell went on to review the following referral and recommendations in further detail. Before jumping into the content of the review, Ms. Buell mentioned that the Town of Martinsburg opted to resubmit this referral for the October County Planning Board meeting, extending the 30-day response period from their September referral submission, upon mutual agreement. Extension follow-up with the Planning Staff was conducted with the applicant because much of the required information was missing. As noted in the technical review, responses have been included in this review and have been shared with the Town of Martinsburg. TOWN OF MARTINSBURG PLANNING BOARD Special Use Permit for the proposed reuse of a 1,200 sq. ft. building located at 7049 State Route 12 from office space to a retail convenience store within the Agricultural Zoning District in the Town of Martinsburg. Tax Map Parcel #228.00-01-06.000 Gurljit Singh – Applicant The Town of Martinsburg Planning Board Secretary provided the following referral documents: 1) General Municipal Referral Form with Agricultural Data Statement; 2) Application to the Planning Board with Land Use Application; 3) SEAF; and 4) Location Map.  Compatibility with Adjacent Uses The proposed action is located on one parcel within the Agriculture Zoning District. The proposed action is not within the Wind Power Overlay Phase 1 or 2, Wellhead Protection Areas, or Water Supply Protection Areas. The proposed reuse of prior office space (commercial use) for a retail convenience store (commercial use) is allowed within the Agricultural Zoning District, subject to a Special Use Permit approved by the Town Planning Board. Since the submission notes that the proposed action will include the sale of tobacco and alcohol, it is important to note that the Town of Martinsburg has opted out of allowing marijuana dispensaries and on-site consumption lounges in its jurisdiction. To ensure that these uses are not commingled with the approved retail convenience store use, it may be beneficial for the Town Planning Board to note this prohibited use as a condition of the Special Use Permit. On September 28, 2026 the applicant confirmed that all retail/commercial sales will be limited to inside the building. This is a key detail that further ensures compliance with the community character. Page 2 of 9 The table below shows that the proposed project appears to meet the district's dimensional standards. Dimensional Standards Lot Area Minimum Lot Frontage Minimum Front Yard Setback Rear Yard Minimum Side Yard Minimum  Agricultural District 1 acre 200 ft 75 ft 25 ft 25 ft Proposed Action 1.7 acres 300 ft Approx. 90 ft Approx. 40 ft Approx. 30 ft Traffic Generation and Effect: The subject property is located on NYS Route 12 between Bealuck Road and Ross Road, and directly across from Markowski Road. There are two (2) driveway egress/ingress for the previously established commercial use. As part of this review, on September 28, the applicant confirmed that the existing driveways will continue to be used; however, they plan to limit use to the southern parking area and driveway. According to estimated measurements taken from GIS, the width of the egress/ingress is estimated to be 26’. According to the submitted Short Environmental Assessment Form (SEAF), the proposed action is not expected to substantially increase traffic above present levels. Although the applicant did not originally provide a traffic egress/ingress plan, on September 28 the applicant provided a handdrawn traffic flow parking plan for the southern parking area, which is currently surfaced with concrete and blacktop.  Protection of Community Character: The proposed action is surrounded by commercial, residential, and agricultural uses along a heavily trafficked NYS corridor. The applicant proposes to reuse the existing structure as a retail convenience store to sell breakfast foods, beer and wine, tobacco, and snacks. As submitted, the proposed use appears consistent with the community character. According to the submitted SEAF, the proposed action will not encroach upon a Critical Environmental Area or adversely affect any known habitat for threatened or endangered species. Review of the NYS EAF Mapper further indicates that the project site does not contain any known threatened or endangered animal species or associated significant habitats. The U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service Official Species List identified the monarch butterfly as a candidate species that may occur within the project area. However, as the submitted referral does not indicate any ground disturbance or vegetation clearing associated with the proposed action, no significant impacts to threatened or endangered species or their habitats are anticipated. Page 3 of 9 Review of the NYS EAF Mapper confirms that the project site does not contain, or is substantially contiguous to, a building, archaeological site, or district which is listed on the National or State Register of Historic Places, or has been determined by the Commissioner of the NYS Office of Parks, Recreation and Historic Preservation to be eligible for listing on the State Register of Historic Places; however, the EAF mapper did identify that the project site, or a portion of it, is located in or adjacent to an area designated as sensitive for archaeological sites on the NY State Historic Preservation Office (SHPO) archaeological site inventory. Upon further investigation, the site was within the boundaries of an archaeological survey completed as part of the Black River to Porter 115kV Transmission Rebuild Project.  Signage: While no plans for signage were submitted with the referral, on September 28, the applicant noted that existing 4’x7’ signage with a replaced business name will be used. Based on this information, the proposed action appears to comply with §240-23, Signs, of the Town of Martinsburg Development Law.  Drainage/Erosion: The SEAF indicates the land disturbance is limited to 0.25 acres, is not within the 100-year floodplain, and does not contain wetlands; however, the NYS EAF Mapper identified that the project site or land adjoining the site contains wetlands or other waterbodies regulated by a federal, state, or local agency. On September 28, the applicant confirmed that the disturbance is limited to the building renovations. Given that the total site disturbance is less than 1 acre, a SPDES General Permit is not required. Upon further investigation using the NYS Environmental Resource Mapper, it appears that the adjoining parcel, owned by The Ramos Irrevocable Trust, hosts a riverine wetland nearly 1,500 feet away from the proposed action.  Parking: While no parking plans were included with the initial referral, the applicant confirmed on September 28 that the existing concrete and asphalt parking area located south of the existing structure will continue to be utilized. No resurfacing or reconfiguration of the parking area is proposed. The anticipated occupancy of the building is approximately 20 persons. A Traffic Flow Plan, submitted on September 28, identifies a total of 18 parking spaces, including three (3) handicap-accessible parking spaces and 15 standard parking spaces. With this information, it appears that the project complies with § 240-24, Parking requirements, as the applicant has now demonstrated that the use will provide off-road parking for all vehicles during peak use periods and will be utilized to avoid backing out onto the public road. Page 4 of 9  Community Facilities: The proposed action will not connect to existing public/private water supply or wastewater utilities.  Lighting: While no plans for the installation or use of existing lighting were submitted with the referral, on September 28, the applicant noted that the proposed action will include upgrades to the existing outdoor lighting with brighter lumens. All outdoor lighting shall be fully shielded and directed downward to minimize glare and light trespass onto adjacent properties and to prevent interference with motorists traveling on NYS Route 12.  Noise Given the proximity of nearby residential properties, operational noise may increase compared with the former office use. Potential sources may include customer vehicle activity, deliveries, refuse collection, and mechanical or refrigeration equipment. Significant noise impacts are not anticipated provided that these activities and equipment are appropriately located, screened, and managed through the Town’s permitting process.  Landscaping and Screening: No landscaping or screening plans were submitted with the referral. On September 28, the applicant confirmed that there will be no additional landscaping or screening of the building or parking area as part of the proposed action. Recommendation: Approve with Conditions The acting municipal body must have a super-majority (majority plus one) vote to disregard the following conditions: 1. All outdoor lighting shall be fully shielded and directed downward to minimize glare and light trespass onto adjacent properties and to prevent interference with motorists traveling on NYS Route 12. Non-Binding Notes: These are used as suggestions and/or advice from the County Planning Board, the municipality is not required to take action, nor is a supermajority vote required. 1. Given the proximity of nearby residences, consideration should be given to locating loading areas, refuse facilities, mechanical equipment, and other potential noise-generating activities away from residential properties where practicable. The Town of Martinsburg Planning Board may also consider whether delivery hours, refuse collection, or other operational activities warrant reasonable limitations to minimize potential impacts on neighboring residences. 2. Since the submission notes that the proposed action will include the sale of tobacco and alcohol, it is important to note that the Town of Martinsburg has opted out of allowing marijuana dispensaries and on-site consumption lounges in its jurisdiction. To ensure these uses are not commingled with Page 5 of 9 the approved retail convenience store use, the Town Planning Board may benefit from noting this prohibited use as a condition of the Special Use Permit. The Board expressed concern that the store appears to have already opened, and Building Code Officer Ben Manning noted that the applicant was told they could not open until they obtained the proper permits. Ms. Buell reminded the Board that the referral and review are based on the submission's content and are limited to convenience-store products, including tobacco and alcohol. With no further discussion, the Board unanimously carried the motion to approve with the identified condition and non-binding notes. Mr. Lehman introduced the second project review. Don Cook moved to approve with conditions, and John Reed seconded. Ms. Schell then reviewed the following referral and recommendations in more detail. TOWN AND VILLAGE OF LOWVILLE PLANNING BOARD Special Use Permit and Site Plan Review for the proposed reuse of an existing garage for retail sales and service, general (personal service), located at 7686 North State Street (State Route 26) in the Village of Lowville. Tax Map Parcel #212.07-05-50.100 Amanda Kraeger – Zehr, Elements Day Spa – Applicant The applicant provided the following project documentation: 1) General Municipal Referral Form; 2) Town and Village of Lowville Planning Board Application Materials; 3) Scope of Work; 3) Correspondence from Lewis County Building & Codes and the Village of Lowville DPW Superintendent; 4) Short Environmental Assessment Form (SEAF) Parts 1 & 2; 5) EAF Mapper Summary Report; 6) Site Photos; 7) DEC Letter of No Jurisdiction; and 8) Parking Plan.  Compatibility with Adjacent Uses: The proposed project is located within the Neighborhood Commercial 1 (NC-1) District, “to provide a pedestrian-oriented, mixed-use (residential and small-scale commercial) transition area between the Village center and surrounding residential areas.” The proposed adaptive reuse of the existing 26’ x 26’ garage into a wellness studio (retail sales and service, general) that complements the existing day spa use in the principal structure appears to be consistent with the intent of the zoning district and is compatible with the surrounding land uses, which include a mix of commercial, residential, and public facilities. With respect to dimensional requirements, the existing garage would be considered nonconforming, as Real Property records indicate it was constructed in 1890. Pursuant to §201-1230, a nonconforming structure Page 6 of 9 may be used for any use permitted in the zoning district in which it is located. Because “retail sales and service, general” is an allowable use in the NC-1 District, the nonconforming status of the structure itself is not anticipated to create zoning concerns.  Traffic Generation and Effect: The proposed project is located on North State Street (State Route 26), which has an Annual Average Daily Traffic (AADT) volume of approximately 8,086 vehicles, with access to the parking lot off Davenport Place. According to the submitted SEAF, the proposed action is not expected to substantially increase traffic beyond existing levels. Based on this review, the project is not anticipated to result in significant traffic impacts.  Protection of Community Character: According to the submitted SEAF, the project site is not located within a Critical Environmental Area, an archaeologically sensitive area, a habitat for threatened or endangered species, or a 100-year floodplain. However, the SEAF indicates that the site is located within or adjacent to a property listed on the State or National Register of Historic Places. The applicant contacted SHPO in advance and received a letter dated September 8, 2026, indicating no adverse impact is anticipated. The submitted SEAF also indicates that the project site is located on or adjacent to a property that has been subject to environmental remediation. According to the New York State Department of Environmental Conservation (NYS DEC) Environmental Remediation Database, this refers to the AMF Trinity Avenue site, which was remediated through the NYS Superfund Program at 5502 Trinity Avenue. As no ground disturbance is proposed as part of this project, impacts related to this prior remediation are not anticipated.  Signage: There is no additional signage proposed for this project. Should any signage be proposed in the future, it should comply with §201-735 C(1) of the Village Zoning Law.  Drainage & Erosion: The submitted SEAF indicates that the proposed project will not result in additional stormwater discharge, and because the project involves no ground disturbance, this is not anticipated to be a concern.  Parking: According to §201-830 G, commercial and business uses require “one space per motor vehicle used directly in the business, plus one space per 350 square feet of business area.” Based on the submitted materials, the principal structure where the day spa currently operates is 4,039 square Page 7 of 9 feet, and with the addition of the 26’ x 26’ wellness studio, that would equate to a total of 4,715 square feet, which would require a total of 14 parking spaces. The submitted parking plan includes 12 parking spaces, including one handicap parking space. Section §201-830 B allows off-street parking to be located off-site, provided it is within 500 feet of the use; it would be available on North State Street and Davenport Place and would certainly make up for the 2 parking spots lacking in the parking lot.  Community Facilities: According to the submitted SEAF, this project would connect to the Village of Lowville water and sewer infrastructure. The applicant contacted the Village of Lowville DPW Superintendent and submitted a letter dated September 10, 2026, indicating that the current infrastructure can accommodate additional use and is not expected to be a concern.  Lighting: According to the submitted materials, the garage has an existing light, and no changes to existing lighting are proposed at this time. Should lighting be added or replaced in the future, it should be downward-directed to prevent spillover onto adjacent properties and comply with §201-1030 of the Village Zoning Law.  Landscaping and Screening: No landscaping is planned at this time. Should landscaping be undertaken in the future, it should comply with §201-1070 of the Village Zoning Law. Recommendation: Approve with Conditions The acting municipal body must have a super-majority (majority plus one) vote to disregard the following conditions: 1. Should any signage be proposed in the future, it should comply with §201735 C(1) of the Village Zoning Law. 2. Should lighting be added or replaced in the future, it should be downwarddirected to prevent spillover onto adjacent properties and comply with §201-1030 of the Village Zoning Law. 3. Should landscaping be undertaken in the future, it should comply with §201-1070 of the Village Zoning Law.
